$comment: Where each detail capture sits in the vehicle, and how the cutout mask
that hides the base splats underneath it is built.
This file is the single source of truth for overlay placement. The
runtime (src/overlay/OverlayManager.js) and the offline mask builder
(tools/build-overlay-masks.js) both read it, which is the point: a mask
baked from one transform and drawn against another misaligns silently,
and the symptom — base splats bleeding through one edge of an overlay —
looks like a dilation problem rather than a stale mask.
src/scene.js holds the hotspot that opens each overlay and refers to it
by id. The prose about why a given capture is placed the way it is lives
Rotation is euler degrees in YXZ order, which is what the in-app align
mode (?align=<id>) prints. A 'quaternion' array [x,y,z,w] is accepted
instead for anything exported from other tooling.
Rebuild the mask after changing anything here: npm run build:masks
